# Project Plan: Village Storefront

**Version:** 1.0
**Date:** 2026-01-02
**Generated By:** Codex GPT-5

<!-- anchor: project-overview -->
## 1. Project Overview

*   **Goal:** Ship a tenant-isolated SaaS commerce platform that marries Shopify-grade merchandising, ConsignCloud-style consignment parity, and Stripe-native payments on a Quarkus modular monolith.
*   **High-Level Requirements Summary:**
    - Multi-tenant Quarkus backend with TenantContext, subdomain/custom-domain routing, PostgreSQL 17 with tenant_id + RLS, and GraalVM native builds.
    - Dual-frontends: Qute + Tailwind + PrimeUI storefront for all customer routes and Vue 3 + PrimeVue + Tailwind admin SPA (plus POS shell) delivered via Quinoa.
    - Core commerce: catalog, variants, inventory, checkout/cart, Stripe-only payments (with provider abstraction), order/fulfillment flows, shipping integrations, loyalty, POS, headless APIs.
    - Consignment parity: consignor onboarding, commission rules, balances/payouts via Stripe Connect, vendor portal, intake workflows, automated notifications.
    - Platform governance: impersonation workflows with audit logging, platform dashboards, reporting/analytics, background job processing via DB-backed queues, observability and compliance.
    - Media processing (images + video) with Thumbnailator/FFmpeg, Cloudflare R2 storage, signed URLs, and autoscaled worker pods.
    - Non-functional: 80% JaCoCo, Spotless, GitHub Actions CI/CD, Kubernetes (k3s) deployment, structured logging, OpenTelemetry, Prometheus, feature-flag governance, rate limiting without Redis.
*   **Key Assumptions:**
    - Existing repo already contains base Quarkus modules and java-project-standards; new work must align with those docs without modifying constraints.
    - Stripe is sole live PSP for MVP; PaymentProvider abstraction must still be coded/tested for future providers.
    - No additional caches beyond Caffeine; rate limiting/token buckets use PostgreSQL + in-memory hybrid per spec.
    - Tenants expect bilingual-ready UI (EN/ES) but only EN shipped Day 1; architecture must support future locales.
    - Kubernetes infrastructure (k3s) with cert-manager and Cloudflare R2 is provisioned by platform ops; plan focuses on app-level manifests/config.
    - Background job runner pattern (DelayedJob) and worker tiers are accepted; no message broker introduction allowed.
    - Reporting consumers rely on precomputed aggregates/exports rather than ad-hoc OLAP; future streaming analytics left for later phases.

<!-- anchor: core-architecture -->
## 2. Core Architecture

*   **Architectural Style:** Layered modular monolith (Quarkus) with bounded-context modules, CDI contracts, and persisted domain events to enable future service extraction without rewriting contracts.
*   **Technology Stack:**
    *   Frontend: Qute + Tailwind CSS + PrimeUI for storefront; Vue 3 + Vite + TypeScript + PrimeVue + Tailwind for `/admin` SPA and POS shell via Quinoa plugin.
    *   Backend: Java 21 + Quarkus (RESTEasy Reactive, Panache, Qute, Scheduler, Kubernetes, Mailer, AWS S3), compiled to GraalVM native images, Maven build with Spotless and JaCoCo 80% gate enforced by SonarCloud.
    *   Database: PostgreSQL 17 shared cluster with tenant_id columns, Row Level Security, monthly partitions for logs, managed via MyBatis Migrations.
    *   Messaging/Queues: Database-backed DelayedJob tables using `SELECT ... FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED`, with worker pods subscribed to CRITICAL/HIGH/DEFAULT/LOW/BULK queues.
    *   Deployment: GitHub Actions → GraalVM native container → Quarkus Kubernetes manifests + Kustomize overlays for k3s; blue/green rollouts with smoke tests.
    *   Other Key Libraries/Tools: AWS S3 SDK (Cloudflare R2), Stripe/Stripe Connect SDKs (plus Stripe Terminal), Quarkus Mailer, FFmpeg CLI, Thumbnailator, MapStruct, Caffeine cache, OpenTelemetry, Prometheus exporters.
*   **Key Components/Services (Component Diagram defined in I1.T3):** Tenant Access Gateway, Identity & Session Service, Catalog & Inventory domain, Consignment module, Checkout & Order Orchestrator, Payment Integration Layer, Loyalty module, POS/Offline processor, Media Pipeline Controller, Reporting projections, Platform Admin backend, Integration adapter layer, Feature toggle service, Background scheduler.
*   **Data Model Overview (ERD refined in I1.T4):** Tenant, StoreUser, Customer, SessionLog, Product, Variant, Category, Collection, InventoryLocation/Level, Consignor, ConsignmentItem, Cart/CartItem, Order/OrderItem, PaymentIntent, Refund, Shipment, ReturnAuthorization, LoyaltyLedgerEntry, FeatureFlag, AuditEvent, BackgroundJob, WebhookEvent, PlatformCommand, GiftCard, StoreCredit, SubscriptionPlan/Contract, PosDevice, MediaAsset/Derivative, RateLimitBucket.
*   **API Contract Style:** RESTful OpenAPI 3.0 spec-first (initial spec skeleton delivered in I2.T4) covering admin/storefront/headless/platform scopes with RFC7807 error payloads, OAuth scopes, feature-flag metadata, and idempotency requirements.
*   **Communication Patterns:** Request-scoped TenantContext, CDI events for tenant resolution/media completion/order lifecycle, REST interactions between modules (even within monolith) to preserve contracts, Stripe/carrier webhooks persisted before processing, SSE/WebSocket notifications for admin/portal updates, background jobs for long-running operations (media, reports, payouts).

## 2.1. Key Architectural Artifacts Planned

*   C4 Component Diagram (PlantUML) – Visualizes major modules/services and integrations; created in `I1.T3`, stored at `docs/diagrams/component_overview.puml`.
*   Canonical ERD (PlantUML) – Documents tenant-scoped schema + support entities; created in `I1.T4`, stored at `docs/diagrams/domain_erd.puml`.
*   Async Processing Sequence Set (Mermaid) – Details DelayedJob lifecycle for media/payout/report queues; drafted in `I2.T6`, refined in `I3.T5`, stored at `docs/diagrams/async_sequences.md`.
*   OpenAPI v3 Spec (YAML) – Spec-first definition for store/admin/platform/headless APIs; initial skeleton in `I2.T4`, evolved across iterations at `api/openapi.yaml`.
*   Tenant Access & RLS Policy Blueprint (Markdown) – Captures tenant resolution logic, RLS templates, safety nets; produced in `I1.T2` at `docs/architecture/tenant_isolation.md`.
*   Checkout & Payment Sequence Diagram (PlantUML) – Shows shipping, loyalty, Stripe flows; authored in `I3.T4` at `docs/diagrams/checkout_sequence.puml`.
*   Deployment & Ops Runbook (Markdown) – Summarizes CI/CD, Kustomize overlays, blue/green, metrics, alerts; produced in `I4.T7` at `docs/operations/runbook.md`.
*   Test Strategy Matrix (Markdown/Table) – Maps unit/integration/e2e coverage per module; drafted in `I1.T6`, updated later at `docs/quality/test_strategy.md`.

<!-- anchor: directives-process -->
## 4. Directives & Strict Process

*   Respect ProjectPlanner protocol: avoid exploratory shell commands (no directory listings), craft internal blueprint before edits, and write artifacts with single atomic commands plus one-line Python verification checks.
*   Anchor every major heading/task with `<!-- anchor: ... -->` comments to support manifest lookups; maintain kebab-case keys matching manifest entries.
*   All plan tasks must cite concrete file targets under the proposed structure, list dependencies, designate agent types, and flag parallel execution opportunities explicitly.
*   Enforce Large-scale planning guidelines: 5 iterations, 5–9 tasks each, each iteration file sized ~140–180 lines, and Section 5–7 coverage aligned with proportion guidance (Iteration content 55–65% of overall plan).
*   Reference existing governance docs (`docs/java-project-standards.adoc`, `.codemachine/inputs/competitor-research.md`) in Inputs to keep downstream agents anchored on standards and competitor context.
*   Integrate verification/testing expectations into tasks rather than isolating them; every feature task must mention required test suites (unit/integration/e2e) and acceptance criteria referencing performance/coverage thresholds.
*   Manifest and artifacts must reside under `.codemachine/artifacts/plan/`; no other output directories may be touched.
*   Feature flags, tenant safety, and compliance (impersonation audits, Stripe-only payments, no Redis) are hard constraints—tasks proposing deviations must add ADR references and fallback plans.
